Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps

Class TitledSwingWindow

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.TitledSwingWindow
public final class TitledSwingWindow extends Object
Presents a conventional Swing JPanel as an integrated 3D desktop window: a Frame3D that hosts the panel on a SwingNode below a real title bar.

Why this exists: a bare SwingNode fills the whole Frame3D with one opaque, pickable quad. Because lg3d mouse events do not propagate to ancestor components by default (Component3D.setMouseEventPropagatable(boolean)), that quad becomes the event source for the entire window - it swallows the BUTTON1 drag that ZLayeredMovableLayout's Component3DMover needs (so the window cannot be moved) and it covers the auto-attached minimize / maximize / close buttons that Frame3DWindowDecoration places at the top-right corner (so they are neither visible nor clickable).

This helper reserves a title-bar strip at the top of the frame, shifts the Swing content down into the remaining area, and makes the strip a pickable, event-propagating drag handle: gestures picked on it travel up to the frame-level listeners of ZLayeredMovableLayout and Frame3DWindowDecoration, so the window keeps every desktop idiom - left-drag the title bar to move it, middle-drag or CTRL+left-drag to rotate it, right-click to flip it to the sticky note - and the standard window buttons sit in the clear strip.

  • Method Details

    • installHostedLookAndFeel

      public static void installHostedLookAndFeel()
      Installs the Swing look-and-feel used by every panel hosted on a SwingNode. This is deliberately the pure-Java cross-platform (Metal) LAF and not the platform/system LAF: on Linux the system LAF is GTK, which is Synth-based, and Synth resolves widget styles through a SynthContext that is null when a component is painted into the SwingNode offscreen BufferedImage rather than a real on-screen peer. Any Synth widget - list, table, radio button, check box, combo box - then throws a NullPointerException from SynthContext.getStyle() during SwingNode.captureNow, which aborts the whole-window repaint and leaves the panel frozen. Metal paints offscreen through DefaultLookup with no SynthContext and is reliable. Call before constructing the panel so its child components are created with the right UI delegates. A failure leaves the current look-and-feel untouched.

    • applySwingFontDefaults

      public static void applySwingFontDefaults()
      Applies the configured Swing UI font (family + size) from DesktopConfig to the UIManager defaults, so hosted panels built afterwards render with the user's chosen font. While the config still holds the built-in default the platform look-and-feel font is left untouched (and any previous override is rolled back to the LAF default). Safe to call again after a configuration change to re-apply live.
